headline: The first psychedelic
at FDA’s door.
dek: Compass Pathways says its psilocybin drug passed two large trials and will finish its FDA filing this year.
photoAlt: A man in glasses holds up a notebook of handwritten notes.
byline: Adonis Men’s Health · Checked Nov 2, 2026 · Clinical review pending

glance.label: Two Phase 3 trials
glance.line: 258 and about 580 adults with treatment-resistant depression, scored at week 6.

glance.label: Filing
glance.line: Rolling application under way; Compass expects to finish it in Q4 2026.

glance.label: Still Schedule I
glance.line: Psilocybin is a Schedule I drug; any launch waits on DEA rescheduling.

body: For decades, [[/psilocybin|psilocybin]], a compound found in so-called magic mushrooms, has been listed by the Drug Enforcement Administration as a Schedule I controlled substance.[^dea] That status may soon be tested. Compass Pathways, a biotechnology company based in London, is sending FDA a new drug application for COMP360, its own synthetic formulation of psilocybin, for treatment-resistant depression.[^aug] In its results release on August 5, 2026, Compass said “Rolling submission and initial review are underway, with some modules of the NDA submitted and on track to complete all modules in Q4”.[^aug] A rolling submission lets a company hand in parts of an application as they are ready.

The application rests on two Phase 3 trials. Both enrolled adults aged 18 or older with major depression whose current episode had not responded to two, three or four different medicines given at an adequate dose and for long enough, and who scored at least 20 on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) at the start.[^ct5][^ct6] The MADRS is described in the trial records as “a 10-item clinician rated scale measuring depression severity”.[^ct5] Each dose was given with psychological support.[^ct5] Compass said participants in the two trials had been in their current episode for more than three years on average.[^aug]

The first trial, COMP005, was placebo-controlled and double-blind. Its registry record lists 258 people enrolled;[^ct5] Compass said 171 received a single 25 mg dose and 87 a placebo, at sites across the United States.[^feb] The main measure was the change in MADRS score at week 6.[^ct5] Compass first reported the result in June 2025: a mean difference between drug and placebo of -3.6 points on the MADRS (95% confidence interval -5.7 to -1.5), with p below 0.001.[^feb] The trial then continued blinded to week 26, with an open-label phase to week 52.[^jul]

The second trial, COMP006, had no placebo arm. Instead, people received two doses three weeks apart of 25 mg, 10 mg or 1 mg, the lowest dose standing in as a control. Compass said 581 people were dosed in North America and Europe (296, 142 and 143 per arm);[^feb] the registry record lists 572 enrolled.[^ct6] On the main measure, again the change in MADRS at week 6, Compass reported in February 2026 a mean difference of -3.8 points between the 25 mg and 1 mg groups (95% confidence interval -5.8 to -1.8), with p below 0.001.[^feb] That release gave no result for the 10 mg group.[^feb]

Then there are the two figures Compass puts first. In both trials, it reported the share of people on 25 mg whose MADRS score had fallen by at least a quarter at week 6. For COMP005 it said “25% of participants in the 25 mg arm achieved a clinically meaningful reduction in MADRS (≥ 25%) at Week 6”;[^feb] for COMP006 the figure was 39%.[^feb] Those numbers are worth reading carefully. They are not remission rates, and they count a smaller drop than a halving of the score. The releases do not give the matching share in the placebo or 1 mg groups. In July, Compass said the people who reached that mark in COMP006 kept the benefit, on average, through at least week 26, and argued that “This compares favorably to the 25% in COMP005 following a single dose”.[^jul] The trials were run differently, so that comparison is the company’s, not a head-to-head test.

On safety, Compass said most side effects came on dosing days, with headache, nausea, anxiety and visual hallucinations the most common.[^jul] It said serious adverse events over 26 weeks in COMP006 occurred in 5.7% of the 25 mg group and 6.3% of the 1 mg group.[^jul] It quoted the chair of the independent safety board as saying there was “no evidence of a clinically meaningful imbalance between treatment arms in suicidality in either study.”[^feb] None of these figures has been independently reviewed: neither registry record had posted results as of November 2, 2026.[^ct5res][^ct6res]

Washington has been moving in the same direction. FDA granted the program Breakthrough Therapy designation in October 2018.[^healio] On April 18, 2026, an executive order told the FDA Commissioner to give national priority vouchers to psychedelic drugs with that designation.[^eo] Six days later FDA announced vouchers for three programs, the first listed as “Psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression.”[^fda] Compass said the same day that it held that voucher, and that FDA had granted its request for a rolling review.[^apr] It said the voucher brings “enhanced communications and a shortened 1-2 month review time”[^apr] once the application is filed.

For men, the stakes are practical. Depression that does not lift after several medicines is hard to treat, and one approved option this lane already covers is [[/esketamine|esketamine]], sold as Spravato, a nasal spray approved for “Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) in adults as monotherapy or in conjunction with an oral antidepressant”.[^spravato] Its label says “SPRAVATO is only available through a restricted program called the SPRAVATO REMS”,[^spravato] and is given only in certified health care settings.[^spravato] Compass has said it expects COMP360 to fit into existing centers that already run multi-hour treatments.[^aug]

What is still unknown is the most important part. FDA has not ruled on the application, and the full trial data have not been published for outside scientists to check. Nobody yet knows how long benefits last past six months in most people, how the drug compares directly with esketamine, or what supervision FDA would demand.

There is also the law. Even with an approval, psilocybin stays in Schedule I until the Drug Enforcement Administration moves it.[^dea] The executive order tells the Attorney General to “initiate and complete review of any product containing a Schedule I substance that has successfully completed Phase 3 clinical trials for a serious mental health disorder”,[^eo] so rescheduling can follow an approval quickly. Compass says launch is expected in the first half of 2027, “subject to FDA approval and following Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) rescheduling.”[^aug] Until then, COMP360 remains, in Compass’s own word, investigational.[^aug]
